Leaders in early years & primary education
Welcome to the Old Palace & Children’s House Federation website
It explains all about our fantastic schools’ partnership and has lots of useful information for parents, staff and visitors
Executive Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to our federation website. Here you will find out more about our federation and how it brings together the excellence of both schools. Children’s House provides outstanding nursery provision for 2-4year olds. Old Palace is a two-form entry primary school, which achieves strong academic outcomes, consistently above the national average.
Both schools have a rich history. Children’s House Nursery is housed in a listed building, which has been serving local children for more than a hundred years. Old Palace was rebuild after the original building was bombed in 1942. It is named after a royal hunting lodge, which once stood on the site. We are proud of our heritage and the high quality education we have delivered to the local community over the decades.
We are very much aware of the responsibility that we have in ensuring that children enjoy coming to school. Are supportive environment helps secure the highest standards of care and education for our children. Strong teaching, first hand experiences and an ambitious curriculum allows each child to succeed by building on what they know, understand and can do.
The importance of physical and emotional health is recognised and we strive to help our pupils and families to adopt healthy habits, including when online. Pupils are taught to develop positive relationships, to value diversity and to care for each other, their community and our world. Visitors often comment on the calm and purposeful environment found at our schools, which reflects the high aspirations we hold for our children.
If you are interesting in applying for one of our schools, please get in touch. We look forward to welcoming you and showing you what makes our schools such special places to learn and grow.
We are committed to providing the highest quality education from the very start of a child’s learning journey. In the early years, our focus is on nurturing curiosity, independence, and a love of learning through play-based experiences in a safe and stimulating environment. As children move into primary education, we build on these foundations with a broad and balanced curriculum that develops knowledge, skills, and creativity. Our aim is to inspire confident, resilient learners who are well-prepared for the next stage of their education and for life beyond the classroom.

Governing body
The School Governing body is responsible for working with the school to ensure that it delivers a high quality education. Together with the head teacher, who is responsible for day-to-day management, they set the school’s aims and policies.
Governors have three main roles:
Committee Membership
Executive Headteacher
Co-opted – Chair of Governor’s
Co-opted – Vice Chair of Governor’s
Mrs Khan (Head of School, Children’s House Nursery) and Mrs Bowley (Deputy Headteacher, Old Palace Primary) also attend Governing Body Meetings as observers.
The Clerk to the Governing Body is Angus Huck.
The Chair of the Governing Body, Charles Barrows, can be contacted c/o Old Palace Primary School, St Leonard’s Street, London, E3 3BT
To provide strategic direction for the school
To ensure accountability
Structure
To support its work, the Governing board has established a Resource Committee and a Curriculum & Standards Committee. There is also a Pay Committee, which is a subgroup of the Resource Committee and a Head Teachers Performance Management Committee, which is made up to the Chair, Vice Chair and one other (non staff/ parent) governor. Other Committees are convened on a needs basis. Please refer to the Terms of Reference for more information. Each governor is also required to serve as a Link Governor. Please see our Governor Code of Conduct for more details of the governor roles and responsibilities.
Terms of reference
Governors Published Details 2025-26
Parent Governor Election
for Children’s House Nursery School
for Mr Atique Alahi father of Ayyub
I would like to put myself forward for the position of Parent Governor for Old Palace Primary School and Children’s House Nursery. I have a strong personal connection to both schools. My son currently attends Children’s House Nursery, and I am also a former pupil of Old Palace Primary School, where I studied until leaving in 1998. Having grown up in the local area and now raising my own family here, I have a genuine interest in supporting our local schools and helping to create the best possible opportunities for children and families. I am the Chief Operating Officer and a founding member of Stroudley Walk Community Organisation (SWCO), a registered charity serving children, young people and families within the Bromley North ward and surrounding areas. As one of the heads of the organisation, I oversee much of our day-to-day operations, programme delivery, partnerships and future development. Through SWCO, we deliver a range of programmes for local children and young people. This includes our holiday programmes through the Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) programme, where we provide activities, sports and meals for children during the school holidays. We have also developed a local football academy, providing regular structured football opportunities for children and young people. Our activities take place across several local sites, including Marner Centre and St Paul’s Way School. Alongside sport, we have delivered educational and employability programmes designed to help young people develop skills, confidence and opportunities for the future. My role within SWCO has given me experience in operations, strategic planning, safeguarding, programme management, funding, partnership working and engaging with local families and organisations. It has also given me a strong understanding of some of the challenges and opportunities facing children and families within our local community. Outside of my charity work, I also have experience in business and entrepreneurship, which I believe would allow me to bring an additional perspective to the governing body, particularly around strategy, operations, financial oversight and organisational development. I would welcome the opportunity to use my experience, local knowledge and community connections to support both Old Palace Primary School and Children’s House Nursery. As both a parent and former pupil, I would be proud to contribute to the schools that have played a part in both my own life and now my son’s. Most importantly, I would approach the Parent Governor role by listening to parents, supporting the leadership of the schools and helping ensure that decisions continue to put the education, wellbeing and future of our children first.
for Mr Muhammad Saif father of Amayah & Musa
I am applying to become a parent governor because I care deeply about the education, safety and wellbeing of the children across Old Palace Primary School and Children’s House Nursery School. As a father of three, with children attending both settings, I have a personal investment in the federation and a clear view of how important the early years and primary stages are in shaping a child’s confidence, curiosity and sense of belonging. I am also a local Tower Hamlets parent whose career has been dedicated to improving opportunities for children and young people. I would welcome the chance to give something back to the schools that play such an important part in my children’s lives and in the wider Bow community. I am particularly drawn to the federation’s commitment to children feeling safe, being included, enjoying learning and developing into confident and resilient learners. Its recognition that parents are partners in their children’s education also strongly reflects how I believe schools and families should work together. Having children at both schools gives me an understanding of the different experiences families have at nursery and primary level, as well as the importance of a positive and joined-up journey between the two. I would bring that parent perspective while always keeping the interests of every child across the federation at the centre of my decisions. I have more than 13 years of experience in youth development, education, mentoring, employability and community-based services across London. I currently work as Director of Youth Development at YouthBuild Ventures UK, where I lead the strategy, quality and delivery of programmes for young people. This includes managing staff, developing services, monitoring performance, working with budgets and partners, and making sure that programmes are safe, inclusive and achieving meaningful outcomes. Across my career, I have helped support more than 1,000 young people, including those facing exclusion, unemployment, safeguarding concerns and other barriers to participation. A major part of my role is safeguarding leadership. As a Designated Safeguarding Lead, I have overseen complex concerns, chaired case-management reviews and worked with schools, families, social care, police, youth justice services and other agencies. I understand the importance of early help, appropriate challenge, clear recording and escalation, and making decisions in the best interests of a child. I would bring this knowledge to the governing body at a strategic level, supporting strong oversight of safeguarding, wellbeing, attendance, inclusion and online safety while respecting the professional responsibilities of school leaders and staff. I believe I could make a useful contribution to the governing body in several connected areas. My safeguarding background would help me review how well policies, reporting arrangements and accountability systems protect children. My programme leadership experience would support the board in considering improvement priorities, the use of evidence, staff capacity, risk and value for money. My work with children, young people and families would also help me bring a grounded perspective on wellbeing, inclusion, special educational needs and disabilities, transitions, attendance and meaningful parent engagement. As someone from a Bangladeshi background who has lived and worked in East London, I understand the strengths of our diverse communities as well as some of the barriers families can face when engaging with services. I would listen carefully to parents, including those who may be less confident in making their views heard, and help the governing body consider whether communication and engagement are accessible and respectful. At the same time, I would remain balanced and evidence-led, recognising that governors must make decisions for the whole school community. If elected, I would approach the role with commitment, accountability and professionalism. I would complete the required induction and training, attend meetings consistently, take on link responsibilities where my skills are useful and continue learning about the early years and primary education context. I would maintain confidentiality, declare any conflicts of interest and support collective decisions once they have been made. Most importantly, I would bring the perspective of a parent who wants every child in the federation to feel safe, known, encouraged and able to succeed. I would be proud to work with fellow governors, staff, parents and the wider community to protect what the schools already do well and to help them continue improving. I believe my combination of parent insight, youth-development leadership, safeguarding experience and knowledge of the local community would allow me to make a thoughtful and reliable contribution as a parent governor.
for Ms Rumina Begum mother of Noah
I wish to stand for the role of Parent Governor because I want to make a positive contribution to our school and help ensure that every child has the opportunity to thrive. As a parent, I care deeply about the school community and would value the opportunity to bring a parent’s perspective to discussions and decisions that affect our children. I would bring strong communication, organisation and listening skills to the role. I am comfortable working collaboratively with others, considering different viewpoints and approaching issues thoughtfully and constructively. I believe it is important for governors to listen to the experiences and concerns of parents, staff and pupils while keeping the wider interests of the school community at the heart of their decisions. If elected, I would be committed to supporting the school’s continued success. I would take the responsibilities of the role seriously, prepare thoroughly for meetings and contribute positively to discussions. I would particularly value the opportunity to support the school in maintaining high standards, providing a positive and inclusive environment for pupils, and ensuring that children are encouraged to achieve their full potential. Most importantly, I would bring enthusiasm, commitment and a genuine desire to support our school. I hope to work constructively with the governing body, staff and fellow parents to help our school continue to develop and provide the best possible experience for all its pupils.
